column3: “Like dung” makes a comparison of the Hebrew description as dung.
“In the dust” specifies rolling; the scattering is not explicit, while “be shattered” expands falling.
“Hear” supplies an imperative before the sound of the cry.
“Silenced” renders the destruction of the peaceful pastures.
“Lion” renders a young lion; “sword of the oppressor” replaces the oppressor’s burning anger, and “the LORD” identifies the final possessive.
